$comment: THE THREE COLOURS A STATE CAN BE, and every word this bench says them with.
See tokens/README.md for why this lives in contracts/ and what may go in it.
WHY IT EXISTS. Five renderers drew the same fact five ways. OcaTable tinted
rows green/red/amber off `_row_state` and drew nothing at all for a row that
had none — which is every row of every capture-point sidecar, so 198 points
read `offline` in flat grey text. DevicesTab painted `identified` BLUE and
everything it did not recognise muted grey, so `declared` and `unknown` were
the same colour as no answer at all. The schematic monitor had a fourth
green and used the brand accent as its amber, which is the colour selection
already means. Nothing was wrong in any one file; the bench simply had no
agreed answer to `is that thing there`.
AND THE FOURTH GREEN IS A SHAPE, NOT AN INCIDENT. The schematic monitor's
extra green above was not a file that copied these three hexes wrongly; it
was a file that copied them NEARLY, which is the more common of the two and
the harder to see -- a census that knows three strings cannot find a fourth
string. `check_state_words.py` measures CIE76 dE in CIELAB against these
three and fails on anything within 17 of one without being it, in any source
that asks the vocabulary a question. It found two more the day it was
written: #ff3344 on a ganged stage box (11.56 from `dead`) and #ff3b3b on a
corrupted DNA strand (10.97), both hand-typed a line away from the call that
would have answered them. 17 sits in the gap below #f4902c, the brand accent
the paragraph below already rules out by name -- 19.59 away, and deliberately
a different colour rather than a near miss. PLAN-626.01.
THE RULE IS THREE BUCKETS AND NOT MORE. Green: something answered. Red:
somebody asked and nothing was there. Amber: neither — written down but
never confirmed, or heard once and not since. Amber is the honest colour for
most of a bench most of the time, and the reason it is not grey is that grey
reads as furniture: `declared` is a claim somebody made, and a claim nobody
has checked is worth looking at.
EVERY WORD BELOW WAS MEASURED IN THIS TREE, not imagined, and here is where:
`offline` 1453 times, `online` 95, `unknown` 71 and `identified` 56 across the
capture-point sidecars and system panels; `declared` and `pending` in
APK:OS/server.py and `unasked` in discovery_sweep.py; `fault` in
build_capture_drawing.py, which stamps it on a rejected row; `up` and `down`
in DockTor/docker scripts/endpoints.sh, which asks the same question
of an address; and `live`/`stale`/`quiet` in the schematic monitor, which asks
a different one -- has THIS SHELL heard it -- and gets the same three colours
because the answer means the same thing to whoever is looking at it.
FIVE OF THEM CAME FROM A SCHEMA RATHER THAN A CENSUS, which breaks the rule
above and is worth saying out loud. `DeviceStatusSchema` in
contracts/src/device-record.ts -- THIS package, two directories away -- is a
closed z.enum of `discovered` `identified` `unresponsive` `stale` `removed`,
and this file named two of them until 2026-09-06 (PLAN-383.01). The other
three fell to the amber default and two of the three were exactly wrong. The
v40 mapping in that same file derives `discovered` from a scan that FOUND the
device and `unresponsive` from one that identified it and then read
connected:0; the registry stamps `stale` after three missed refresh windows
and `removed` after ten. So `discovered` is something answered -- green --
and `unresponsive` and `removed` are absences that were actually tested for
-- red. `stale` is the untested one and stays amber, which it already was.
check.sh statewords now reads that enum as a declared source and FAILS on a
word it names that this file does not; the JSON census below never could,
because a z.enum is not a status string in a panel.
AND SIX MORE CAME FROM A SECOND SCHEMA, one file over. `AgentStatusSchema`
in contracts/src/heartbeat.ts is the status of a retained AgentHeartbeat --
the document that answers `is that AGENT there` the way the enum above
answers it for a device. This file named `online` and `offline` and nothing
else until 2026-09-06 (PLAN-417.01). Unlike the device three, none of the
other four was obviously the wrong colour, so each was ruled on its own
producer rather than on the word:
`degraded` -> DEAD. Baremetal.Manager/agent_supervision.py health() mints
it, and only it, when an agent expected_up() says should be running is
measurably not -- and has been started before, so this is not a cold node.
That is an absence somebody asked about, which is what red means here. Its
own docstring rules out green: reporting `online` because the SUPERVISOR is
fine `would be the ghost the heartbeat contract exists to prevent`. Amber is
wrong for the other reason -- amber says nobody asked, and health() asked.
`starting` -> KINDA, and named rather than left to fall through. health()
returns it only when every down agent has starts == 0: nothing has come up
yet, so nothing has answered and nothing has been found missing.
`stopping` -> KINDA. health() returns it on shutting_down. The beat still
arrives, so it is not an absence; but green invites a reader to route work
to a process that is on its way out, which is the same ghost by a slower
road.
`stub` -> KINDA. orchestrator/src/mqtt.rs publishes it retained for the
four protocols with no implementation behind them (nmos, rest, mdns,
websocket), and Protocol-rest/src/lib.rs asserts STATUS == "stub" in a unit
test so that implementing it cannot pass silently. It is `declared` with the
claim inverted -- a declared ABSENCE -- and it belongs beside it in amber.
Red was considered and refused for the reason expected_up() gives about a
different word: a fault that is permanent and intended trains an operator to
ignore the colour.
A THIRD ENUM IN THE SAME PACKAGE IS DELIBERATELY NOT A SOURCE.
LegacyVisaRecordV0 in device-record.ts declares z.enum(['found',
'identified']) and `found` is not below. It is a v40 wire shape schema'd for
extraction only; mapV40VisaRecord converts `found` -> `discovered` before
anything draws it, so it cannot reach a renderer, and the census finds it in
no tracked JSON. Naming it would cost four renderer copies a word none of
them may draw. The reasoning is at the ENUMS list in check_state_words.py.
AND FOUR CAME FROM THE CENSUS ITSELF, which is the way this file was
supposed to grow all along. check.sh statewords collected every liveness
value in the tracked JSON, and sixteen of them had no colour here; the
report was advisory, so nobody drove it down and it grew. Twelve of the
sixteen turned out not to be liveness at all (PLAN-418.01) and are ruled
on at NOT_LIVENESS in check_state_words.py. FOUR were, and they are these,
all authored in the SPOG route tree under Softapps/TOUCH/spog/Routes:
`ok` -> GOOD. 181 hits, the healthy word of every route source and
destination. SPOG's own isFaultStatus() in domain/routing-core reads
exactly `OK` as not-faulted and everything else as faulted, so this is
not a guess about the word -- it is the rule the app already runs on.
`no connection` -> DEAD. 001_VIDEO SB 101.json. A stage box that was
asked for and is not answering: an absence somebody tested for.
`lost clock` -> DEAD. 002_AUDIO SB 101.json. It was locked and is not
now, which is the same tested absence one layer down -- the box is
reachable and the signal it carries is not usable.
`locked` -> GOOD. 001_PTP Grandmaster.json. A grandmaster that has
disciplined is the single most affirmative thing a clock can say, and
SPOG draws it TODAY as a fault with a warning triangle, because its
isFaultStatus() knows one healthy word and `LOCKED` is not it. That is
PLAN-484.01; naming the word here is what the fix read.
AND FOUR MORE CAME FROM A THIRD ENUM, WRITTEN IN RUST. `AGENT_STATES` in
contracts/rust/src/agent_state.rs is what a PROTOCOL HUNTER says about its
own ability to see the network -- published retained on
APK.audio/System/Protocols/{proto}/Agent/state, read as a word by the
orchestrator, by launch.py and by the shell's clock reader. It is the third
closed vocabulary in this package and the gate could not see it until
2026-09-06 (PLAN-485.01), because ENUMS was written for `z.enum` and this
one is a `const [&str; 4]`. It is a SOURCE for the same reason the other
two are and the generated Rust in contracts/rust/src/gen/ is not: it is
where these four words are DECIDED, with no TypeScript twin anywhere.
Each was ruled on its producer, the way the heartbeat six were:
`listening` -> GOOD. AgentState::Listening is `every transport this agent
wanted is open`. The agent was asked and it answered, which is green.
`unavailable` -> DEAD. `Nothing opened. The agent is running and can see
nothing.` The agent tried every transport and every one failed, so this
is a conclusion it reached about its own host -- an absence that was
actually tested for, which is exactly what red means here.
`partial` -> KINDA, and this is the one that could have gone either way.
Some transports opened and some did not; is_hunting() returns true, so it
is not an absence and red is wrong. Green is wrong for the reason
`stopping` is not green above: it invites a reader to trust a capture
that is missing half its transports, and `no gPTP clocks` and `could not
listen for gPTP` are the two answers this word exists to keep apart.
Amber is the honest one -- the thing is partly there and nobody can say
more than that from a colour.
`under_test` -> KINDA. PLAN-459.01 added it for an agent an operator has
withdrawn onto the workbench; its own doc comment says `NOT a fault:
nothing here is broken`, and is_withdrawn() exists to keep it out of the
degraded count. Green is wrong the other way -- its findings are
explicitly not to be believed while somebody is working on it. Amber says
nobody can say, and nobody can, until the person holding it is finished.
AND ONE CAME FROM NEITHER A SCHEMA NOR THE CENSUS: IT IS MINTED IN
JAVASCRIPT AT READ TIME. The shell's DataBus ledger, bus-ledger.js, sets
`record.status = 'cleared'` when a retained heartbeat arrives with an EMPTY
payload, and busAgentState() returns it AHEAD OF EVERY OTHER BRANCH. No
tracked JSON carries the word and no enum declares it, so the JSON census
and the enum reader were both blind to it and it drew amber by fall-through
for as long as it existed -- the same blind spot StatusLight.jsx hid in,
one layer down. check.sh statewords now reads the string literals a DECLARED
JavaScript reader can return, a third source beside the renderer copies and
the enums, which is how it was finally seen. PLAN-470.01.
`cleared` -> KINDA, and the PRODUCER settles it rather than the word.
Every Last Will in this tree publishes a JSON document saying `offline`,
retained -- agent_supervision.py:995, spacenavigator_probe.py:858,
linux_desktop_monitor.py:336 and bus_watch.py:253. An agent that DIES
therefore says `offline`. A zero-length retained payload is something
else entirely, and the only things in this tree that publish one at an
agent are hand tools: Storage:MQTT/clear-retained-status.py --clear, and
the DataBus window's own purge control. So `cleared` is never a
measurement OF the agent -- it is the answer being withdrawn by an
operator, and the agent was not asked anything. Red is wrong and would
be actively misleading: red already means `offline` here, which is
exactly what a death looks like, so painting a withdrawn record the same
colour reports a death nobody observed. Amber's own role text is this
case verbatim -- heard once and not since.
AND THE TIMELINE BAND'S THREE FRESHNESS WORDS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT HERE.
mount-timeline-strip.js's timelineFreshness() stamps `unstamped`, `stale`
and `fresh` on the provenance chip under the key `state`, so the census
-- which reads `status` and `_row_state` -- cannot see any of the three.
`stale` is named above and the spelling coinciding is a coincidence rather
than a reuse; the other two are ruled at NOT_LIVENESS in
check_state_words.py, because they answer how old the DRAWING is and not
whether anything on this bench replied. The reader is declared to the gate
all the same, so a FOURTH freshness word is a decision somebody takes
rather than a default it fades into. PLAN-418.01.
`up` AND `ok` NOW MEAN GOOD HERE AND ARE STILL REFUSED THERE, and that is
not a collision. agent_state.rs's header names `up`, `ok` and `running` as
the spellings a fourth adopter might reach for instead of `listening`, and
AgentState::parse returns None for all three. This file and that one decide
different questions: this one decides what a word is DRAWN as, that one
decides what a word is ADMITTED as. An agent that published `up` would draw
the same green as `listening` and still be an unparseable publisher outside
the contract -- so the colour agreeing costs nothing and the parser refusing
is what catches it. Neither word belongs in NOT_LIVENESS: both answer `is
that thing there` where they were measured.
TWO OF THESE WORDS HAVE A SPACE IN THEM and that is why the four renderer
copies quote those two keys. A vocabulary is what the bench SAYS, not what
fits an identifier; check_state_words.py's WORD_RE reads a quoted key for
exactly this reason.
A WORD THAT IS NOT HERE IS AMBER, and that is deliberate: an unrecognised
state is exactly `nobody can say`.
WHAT HOLDS IT NOW. The gate the paragraphs above describe was deleted with
`.apk.scripts/` on 2026-09-10 (2240c51e5) and REWRITTEN against today's tree
(LOOSE-apk-audio-about-360-comments): `check.sh statewords` runs
`check_state_words.py` again and holds the four renderer copies (tones and
word map exactly), the three closed enums, the minted readers and the JSON
census. What it does NOT carry is the hex census, the near-miss ladder and
the selector census: a renderer that invents its own palette -- a fourth
green spelled as a hex -- still reaches the bench with nothing saying no.
The paragraphs above are kept because each records a DECISION -- why
`degraded` is red, why `stub` is amber, why `found` is not a word here.
THE THREE TONES BELOW ARE FIXED ACROSS EVERY COLOUR-VISION PALETTE, AND
THAT IS A RULING RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. SPOG ships seven palettes, four
of them marked cvdSafe, and colour-engine.ts remaps each one's alarm/ok/
onair onto <html>. It does NOT remap these three, and must not: this file is
a cross-language contract with four renderer copies -- a Rust crate, a
Python server and two TypeScript apps -- and three of the four have no
operator, no palette setting and nothing to read one out of. A verdict that
changed hex per browser preference would stop being one answer to `is that
thing there`. The palette's alarm is also not the same claim: lcars.css says
in its own words that --state-alarm is this console's themable alarm CHROME
-- the CUT button, the layout lock, the log-out tile -- and a skin accent
sharing a hex with a verdict is exactly the confusion the amber below is
already kept away from #f4902c to avoid. PLAN-791.01.
WHAT THAT RULING COSTS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Simulated with the
Machado 2009 severity-1.0 matrices and compared as CIEDE2000, `dead` against
`good` is 69.7 dE to normal vision, 12.9 protanopic, 7.3 deuteranopic, 67.5
tritanopic -- and 0.0 achromatic: both fall on #8c8c8c, a WCAG contrast of
1.01:1. Red and green here are not merely hard to tell apart without colour
vision, they are THE SAME PIXEL. `kinda` is the only one of the three that
separates in grey, and only just (7.4 dE, 1.33:1).
SO COLOUR IS NEVER THE ONLY CHANNEL, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE FIXED TRIPLE
SAFE. Every draw that spends a tone pairs it with something a greyscale
screen still carries: faultTag() gives `dead` a leading warning triangle,
gives `kinda` the bare word with no triangle, and gives `good` no badge at
all; lcars.css runs faultPulse on a corrupted strand, which is motion. A
future draw that separates these three by hue alone is a regression against
this paragraph even though every hex in it came from this file.
AND IF THE RULING IS EVER REVERSED, the numbers to beat are above. Two of
the four cvdSafe palettes would genuinely help on the pair that matters
most -- Okabe-Ito's alarm/ok separate 20.5 dE deuteranopic and IBM Carbon's
15.7, against these tones' 7.3 -- and two would not: Paul Tol's is 8.2 and
Classic LCARS's 15.1. That is the honest case for the other answer, and it
is written here so the next reader argues with a measurement.
AND `absent` -> KINDA, ruled once for its two minters (SDK/contracts audit,
CC-02/OS-04, 2026-10-30). OS/Scanalyzer/puck/relay-puck-to-cloud.js mints
it (OS.PUCK_ABSENT) for a bench whose SpaceNavigator branch carries no
retained status at all, and OS/SpaceMouse/mount-space-mouse.js draws it
after four seconds of a connected bus with nothing on that branch. Both say
the same thing in their own words: `a fact about the bench, not a fault --
nothing has failed`. It is never published. Red is refused for the reason
`stub` is amber: an optional peripheral that is simply not attached is a
permanent, intended state, and painting it red trains an operator to
ignore red. Green is refused because nothing answered. Amber, nobody can
say more -- until a probe publishes, which lights the same window green.

good.role: Something answered. A poke got a reply, a scan identified it, a topic arrived.

dead.role: Somebody asked and nothing was there. An absence that was actually tested for.

kinda.role: Neither. Declared and unconfirmed, or heard once and not since. NOT the brand accent -- #f4902c already means selection, and a state must not look like a choice.
